name: Open Marxism
summary: Open Marxism is a non-deterministic reading of Marx, consolidated in Britain in the Open Marxism volumes of the 1990s, that treats capital, state, money and law as fetishised forms in which an open-ended class struggle exists. It rejects closed Marxisms (base and superstructure, laws of history, the vanguard party, state socialism) and treats class as an antagonism to be abolished, not an identity to affirm. Its politics is anti-state and anti-party: revolution as self-emancipation here and now through councils, assemblies and refusal, without taking power, and with an internationalism that rejects nationalism and personified anti-capitalism.
scope: The British-centred school of Werner Bonefeld, Richard Gunn, Kosmas Psychopedis, John Holloway and the Common Sense circle: Open Marxism vols 1-3 (1992-95), Holloway's Change the World Without Taking Power (2002/2005) and Global Capital and the National State, and Bonefeld's later critical theory (Critical Theory and the Critique of Political Economy, 2014, read through reviews quoting it, and his essays on antisemitism). It excludes the earlier Arguments and Praxis uses of the label and structuralist, analytical and party-state Marxism. Social, cultural, religious and foreign-policy statements are mostly outside what these texts discuss, so those answers are low-confidence inferences from the core principles.

furtherReading.note: Overview of the school's origins, thinkers and quarrel with orthodox Marxism.

furtherReading.note: The founding volume, with the editors' case for open rather than closed Marxist categories.

furtherReading.title: Change the World Without Taking Power, John Holloway
furtherReading.note: The school's best-known book, on power-to, power-over and revolution without seizing the state.

furtherReading.note: An accessible spoken clash between the anti-state and the Leninist positions.

keyFigures.name: John Holloway
keyFigures.role: Open Marxist theorist of fetishism and anti-power; author of Change the World Without Taking Power and co-editor of Open Marxism 3.

keyFigures.name: Werner Bonefeld
keyFigures.role: Co-editor of the Open Marxism volumes and theorist of the state as the political form of capitalist social relations.

sources.title: Open Marxism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Origins (Axelos, Agnoli, the CSE), key thinkers, influences and the school's stance on the vanguard party, base/superstructure, class and councils.

sources.title: Social constitution and the form of the capitalist state
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld (Open Marxism vol. 1, 1992)
sources.usedFor: The state as a moment of the class antagonism, rights and law as forms of exploitation, formal equality, the world market, crisis and the rejection of objective laws.

sources.title: Open Marxism 2: Theory and Practice (editors' introduction)
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld, Richard Gunn, Kosmas Psychopedis (eds.)
sources.usedFor: Unity of theory and practice, rejection of determinism and capital-logic, no inescapable lines of development.

sources.title: Debate between John Holloway and Alex Callinicos: Can we change the world without taking power?
sources.author: John Holloway, Alex Callinicos (World Social Forum 2005)
sources.usedFor: Holloway on the state, party, elections, the citizen/foreigner split, councils with recallable delegates, revolution here and now and armed resistance.

sources.title: Open Marxism 1: Dialectics and History (editors' introduction)
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld, Richard Gunn, Kosmas Psychopedis (eds.)
sources.usedFor: Meaning of openness, critique of closed causal or teleological determinism and of the Leninist party, the state as a form of class struggle, self-emancipation.

sources.title: Open Marxism 3: Emancipating Marx (introduction and contents)
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld, Richard Gunn, John Holloway, Kosmas Psychopedis (eds.)
sources.usedFor: Freeing Marx from scientific Marxism, rejection of value-neutral social science, Dalla Costa on women's unwaged work, humans as ends not resources.

sources.title: Change the World Without Taking Power: The Meaning of Revolution Today
sources.author: John Holloway (Pluto Press, 2002/2005)
sources.usedFor: Power-to versus power-over, the state and the party, nationalism, fetishism, money, science, class as struggle against being classified, revolution as a question, private property, technology.

sources.title: Moving Against-and-Beyond (Epilogue to Change the World Without Taking Power)
sources.author: John Holloway
sources.usedFor: Councils and the commune of communes, mandar obedeciendo and recall, rejection of the working-class state, representation, markets and cooperatives, violence and armed defence, money and labour.

sources.title: Global Capital and the National State
sources.author: John Holloway (Capital & Class, 1994)
sources.usedFor: National states as moments of global capital, competition among states for capital, nationalism and the citizen/foreigner divide, socialism as a global project, rejection of dependency theory.

sources.title: Interview with Werner Bonefeld (Shift magazine, 2009)
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld
sources.usedFor: Rejection of the good industry/bad finance split, bailouts, regulation, class as a critical concept, democracy of the street, the commune of the free and equal.

sources.title: Antisemitism and the (modern) critique of capitalism
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld
sources.usedFor: Antisemitism as personification of capital, conspiracy thinking, blood-and-soil national community, critique of anti-imperialist excuses for antisemitism.

sources.title: Revolutionary Writing: Common Sense Essays in Post-Political Politics (foreword and preface)
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld (ed.)
sources.usedFor: Capital's forms as perverted human relations, a society of the free and equal where humanity is purpose not means, democracy of the living.

sources.title: Bonefeld on Critical Theory and the Critique of Political Economy (review)
sources.author: Christian Lotz, Radical Philosophy Review 18:2 (2015)
sources.usedFor: Quoted claims of Bonefeld's 2014 book: the state as political form of capitalist relations, law and police, the strong neoliberal state, permanent primitive accumulation, class as objective category, history without telos.

sources.title: Review of Werner Bonefeld, Critical Theory and the Critique of Political Economy
sources.author: Paul Cammack, Progress in Political Economy (2016)
sources.usedFor: Bonefeld on ordoliberalism and the coercive state behind market liberty, rejection of economic laws, the false split of productive nation and finance, the regressive enemy's-enemy logic.

sources.title: On How to Make Adorno Scream: Some Notes on John Holloway's Change the World Without Taking Power
sources.author: Marcel Stoetzler
sources.usedFor: Account and critique of Holloway on power, identity, class, nationalism and anti-imperialism.

sources.title: An Anarchist Review of Change the World Without Taking Power
sources.author: Wayne Price
sources.usedFor: Holloway's quoted claims on the state as a capitalist form, the Soviets, councils and the commune of communes, revolution as process, the Zapatistas and violence.

sources.title: A Critical Review of John Holloway's Change the World Without Taking Power
sources.author: Phil Hearse
sources.usedFor: Trotskyist critique showing how Holloway's rejection of the vanguard party and of the fight over government differs from Leninist strategy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a theme in the sources; an anti-capitalist current would back decommodified care, though it distrusts the state as its provider, hence only mild agreement inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Bonefeld treats welfare-state gains as struggle-won but integrating; adherents would support the wage fight yet see reform as accommodation, so they split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Holloway writes that when doing is articulated through the market the doers lose control of it, and Bonefeld treats the market and money as fetishised forms of class domination rather than efficient allocators.

public-ownership.rationale: Bonefeld rejects the social-democratic and state-socialist view of class as a market position fixed by redistribution, and the school calls state socialism a closed form, so nationalisation is not the aim despite the anti-capitalism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources do not discuss taxation; redistribution through the state is both welcome as a gain and dismissed as reformist integration.

unions-good.rationale: Workers' self-organisation is central, but unions as institutions often channel struggle into capital's terms; inferred mild support.

property-fundamental.rationale: Holloway calls the definition of the done as private property a negation of the sociality of doing, and Bonefeld says law mediates exploitation through property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Bonefeld doubts that responsible regulation can resolve capitalist crisis, while the movement opposes corporate power, so no clear policy position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is a product of past class struggle in Bonefeld's account; cutting it is austerity against labour, though adherents also critique welfare's disciplining role.

worker-ownership.rationale: Holloway praises occupied factories in Argentina but warns that producing for the market or orienting to the state limits them, so ownership of firms is only a partial step.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from hostility to the state as an instrument of domination and the emphasis on autonomy; no source discusses terrorism or surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from libertarian anti-state, anti-discipline stance of autonomist-influenced theory.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust handing the state coercive power, though they oppose racism, so inferred weak disagreement.

strong-leader.rationale: Holloway's whole case is against power-over and against representatives taking our place, which rules out a strong leader bypassing others.

state-harmful.rationale: Holloway calls the state a process of determination on behalf of others that is incompatible with self-determination, and the school looks to replacing it with councils rather than a better state.

limit-guns.rationale: No source addresses gun control; adherents are anti-state yet not pro-gun as such, so genuinely unstated.

empower-police-military.rationale: Bonefeld stresses the police and law-making violence as the state's means of containing class antagonism, which the critique opposes.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would split between decriminalisation and treating it as commodified labour.

decide-locally.rationale: Holloway's model starts from neighbourhood assemblies and communes federated upward, so decisions are pushed toward those affected rather than a national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from view that crime and punishment are products of social relations rather than individual defects.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; critique of social forms and unpaid reproductive work from Dalla Costa influence implies scepticism of the traditional family as foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory orientation, though marriage as state institution is viewed critically.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory, autonomy-centred outlook.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from materialist critique, with no stated stance on public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory orientation, with the caveat that race and class are not separated in a single-antagonism theory.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the view that social categories are historically constituted forms rather than natural facts.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Holloway calls nationalism an inevitable complement of the logic of power and urges going beyond identities, though cultural practices as such are not attacked.

gradual-change.rationale: Holloway calls for revolution here and now rather than when the time is right, and the editors reject reformist Marxism along with determinism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Holloway rejects all discrimination against foreigners and treats the citizen/foreigner distinction as a fragmenting state form.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; international institutions are state forms in the world market, so more power for them is unlikely to be welcomed.

free-trade.rationale: Bonefeld calls the world market the most developed form of abstract labour, to which national economies are subordinate, so free trade is a mode of domination, not a universal benefit.

nation-first.rationale: Holloway argues socialism must be a global project and that recomposing labour requires rejecting nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to states as instruments of domination, so military action by states is doubted.

open-borders.rationale: Holloway calls the state's division of people into citizens and foreigners racist and holds that anti-racist politics must be anti-state.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; critique of capital's endless valorisation points toward limits, but adherents do not state an environmental programme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; support for action is likely but doubt that capitalist states can deliver it, so the answer is unstated and split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Holloway, following Marx, treats machinery as capital's weapon against workers' revolts and locates the basis of a different society in social cooperation, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No source touches energy policy and no principle decides it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Holloway's book is a defence of revolution understood as an unending process of self-emancipation rather than a seizure of power.

experts-over-public.rationale: Holloway rejects the vanguard model of knowledge brought from outside and calls for a dialogical politics.

central-planning.rationale: The school rejects state socialism and the party-state as forms of domination, and Holloway's commune of communes is self-determination, not planning from a centre.

socialized-markets.rationale: Holloway says cooperatives that produce for the market face the same constraints as capitalist firms, so worker or public ownership does not redeem market exchange.

land-value-tax.rationale: Taxation reform is not discussed and no principle settles it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; a redistributive reform that adherents neither prioritise nor oppose.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; may be seen as a gain against capital or as a state integration device, so adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: National protection frames workers as part of national capital; the world-market, internationalist view suggests disagreement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy reproduces the statist form that is criticised, so it is disfavoured.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property is understood as a form of exploitation, so spreading it is not a solution; not discussed explicitly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Holloway's goal is a world not ruled by money and a drive against labour, and Bonefeld's emancipation means abolishing abstract labour so that time is not money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would reject market money as much as state money, so they reject the premise of this statement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bonefeld describes reformism and welfare structures as integrating labour into the reproduction of capital, which state-recognised bargaining bodies would deepen.

one-party-rule.rationale: Holloway says the party form already contains the substitution of class by party and party by leader, and the editors reject Leninist and Stalinist dialectical materialism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; hereditary rule conflicts with the anti-hierarchy, self-determination commitments.

democracy-best.rationale: Holloway rejects representative democracy for direct democracy, so adherents split on democracy as a general form of government.

direct-votes.rationale: Holloway opposes representative democracy and favours "some form of direct democracy," though through assemblies rather than referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Holloway names the council, assembly or commune as his key organisational reference, and the school prefers councils to parliament and state.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; self-determination is favoured but nation-building is not.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; strongly against by egalitarian, anti-hierarchy logic.

political-violence-never.rationale: Holloway says acts like terrorism do nothing to create a better world, but he accepts that some armed defence, as with the Zapatistas, may be necessary.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalism and critique of nationalism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from materialist and anti-state views.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the critique of state law as a form of capital and from the secular materialism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private security is capital's own rule exercised without a state, so it is rejected even more than public provision.

military-superiority.rationale: Holloway treats states as competing fragments of global capital and wants socialism as a global project, so national military superiority is no goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bonefeld criticises the organic blood-and-soil idea of national community, and Holloway rejects nationalism and the state's racist ordering of people.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bonefeld states that structures exist only as modes of existence of class struggle, and the OM2 editors call class the power that drives history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Class abolition implies equality, but adherents avoid distributive formulas centred on the state, so mild agreement.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Zapatismo is cited approvingly as autonomous self-organisation, which implies support for indigenous autonomy; the specific claim is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; support in principle but reparations are a state-to-state mechanism, so unstated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; supranational blocs defined by religion or civilization conflict with class internationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Bonefeld and the OM3 editors reject the possessive individual of bourgeois theory and want humans as ends in a society of the free and equal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Formal rights are criticised as forms of domination, but duties to community ahead of individuals are also not endorsed; inferred disagreement.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on the value of nature.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; population limits are a state-imposed, scientistic fix, which is disfavoured.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; capital is critiqued but industrial civilization is not rejected as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Anti-scientism and the critique of capital's drive to revolutionise production imply scepticism toward acceleration.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources never discuss body or mind technology; adherents have no settled view and could see both emancipation and commodification in it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Technocratic algorithmic rule is the opposite of self-determination and an alienated form of state.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to state control and surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: The school's open dialectic aims to move against-and-beyond existing forms, and Holloway treats tradition and identity as things to overcome.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Theory against society is critical; pragmatic dismissal of theory conflicts with the unity of theory and practice.

direct-action.rationale: Holloway rejects winning state power through elections and favours self-organised refusal and cracks here and now.

means-match-ends.rationale: Holloway writes that the notion of capturing power in order to abolish power has failed, and asks that struggle move against-and-beyond by prefiguring self-determination.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; no source holds this, and Marxist tradition values the human productive power capital creates.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not stated in the sources; the aim of abolishing labour and class implies it in Marxist terms.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Classic Marxist communist principle, but the sources themselves do not state it, so inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Bonefeld pictures emancipation as a society of human purposes in place of the rule of value, and Holloway sets useful doing against abstract labour for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Bonefeld treats labour as the substance of value and the class relation as one of exploitation and violence, with primitive accumulation as permanent.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Holloway explicitly rejects the idea of a working-class state and says we struggle against being working class, so a class dictatorship is not the route to abolishing classes.

collective-farming.rationale: No source discusses agriculture; the anti-statist stress on voluntary self-organisation cuts against both compulsion and collective mandates, so it is left split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; imperialism theory is not a distinctive Open Marxist theme, which stresses open class struggle over inevitability.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject the premise of a natural private-property entitlement.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberal limits on the state are seen as fetishised forms, so only mild disagreement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are criticised as forms of bourgeois society; collective subjects are not denied.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; state coercion into the military conflicts with anti-state commitments.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; focus is on collective self-organisation, not individual exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers is a market logic that is the target of critique.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bonefeld calls formal freedom and equality the mode of existence of exploitation, treating the doubly free labourer as free only in form.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; power is located in capitalist social relations rather than in cultural elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; rejects naturalised social categories and positivism.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation integrates classes under the state, which is opposed.

total-state.rationale: The state is the political form of capital and Holloway calls it incompatible with self-determination, so state direction of all life is the opposite of the aim.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist myths are alien to an internationalist critique.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; imperial expansion is opposed by the internationalist stance.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; feudal hierarchy conflicts with the egalitarian orientation.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; unfree labour contradicts self-determination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Holloway says knowledge-about is power-over and OM3 rejects value-neutral social science, though the school is a critique of appearances, not a relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Bonefeld appeals to a society where humanity is purpose not means, yet the school rejects ahistorical rational foundations, so its answer is unclear.

single-common-good.rationale: The antagonism between capital and labour denies a single common good in capitalist society.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The school opposes national states as such, but Bonefeld attacks anti-imperialists who single out Israel as a Jewish state, so adherents would split on this framing.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources say nothing on diaspora or citizenship rules; the critique of state citizenship pulls one way and solidarity with the displaced the other.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nation-building project the sources never take up; adherents are indifferent to it as such.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Support for self-organisation of workers' councils and assemblies suggests agreement, though within capitalism it is a limited reform.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-based public provision is a commodity form; not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; austerity is opposed as an attack on labour in the crisis.

economic-freedom.rationale: Bonefeld argues that market liberty is produced and policed by a coercive state, so economic freedom is a form of class rule, not a foundation of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; moral hierarchy by rulers conflicts with self-determination.

national-self-determination.rationale: Holloway lists national self-determination among the confusions that replace the drive to social self-determination with a fixed identity.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; state military force is disfavoured.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-positivism and "reconstructed" Hegel mean a non-scientistic reason; stance on faith is not stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Holloway names discrimination against foreigners among the state practices that fragment the working class and must be rejected.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Holloway frames struggle against labour; compulsory work disciplines labour for capital.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bonefeld calls class an objective antagonism of capitalist reproduction and the aim is to dissolve class society, not partnership between classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; no support for futurist destruction of culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Bonefeld calls the logic that an enemy's enemy is a friend entirely regressive and criticises anti-imperialist politics that sets dominated nations against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Holloway states that recomposing labour as a class requires rejecting nationalism and discrimination against foreigners, since states are fragments of one global capital.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory outlook.

ban-interest.rationale: Bonefeld rejects the split between bad finance and good industry and links the critique of money as more money to antisemitic personification, so banning interest misdirects the critique.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; fully opposed by egalitarian logic.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Holloway explicitly criticises the orthodox view of the state as an instrument of the ruling class, treating it instead as one moment of fetishised capitalist social relations; Bonefeld calls it a moment of the class antagonism.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; only inferred scepticism of capital's accumulation drive.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; critique of the state's national logic.

elite-replacement.rationale: Bonefeld treats conspiracy theories of an invisible abstract power as personifications of capital, and Holloway rejects anti-foreigner politics.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary electoral design is outside the concern of an anti-parliamentary stance.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; national mission is alien to internationalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Influences include Dalla Costa; structural domination by gender is plausible but not explicitly stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; critique is of the state form, not individual corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; eugenics fully opposed by egalitarian logic.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; mild support from critique of state violence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Bonefeld reads Adam Smith's liberal state as police order securing market freedom and property, which is the form his critique targets.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Never addressed, but an anti-racist, emancipatory theory would reject state or social pressure against mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formal equality is critiqued as a form masking exploitation, but equal worth is assumed in the emancipatory aim, so mild agreement.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Holloway argues socialism must be global because national states are moments of global capital, though he rejects the statement's idea of revolution as seizing states.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources never discuss settler colonialism, and adherents' class-centred framing leaves the classification open.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law reform is not discussed; a critique of state law as a capital form leaves adherents without a clear stance.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; state restriction of belief disfavoured.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; religious state law is disfavoured.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; secular materialism is assumed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Open Marxism rejects state socialism and its aim is dissolving the state, so a strengthening socialist state is rejected.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not addressed; social-contract legitimacy is a bourgeois form.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export drives treat the national economy as a competitor in the world market, a framing that Bonefeld's world-market analysis does not endorse; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority is state coercion against people and is inferred to be rejected under internationalist egalitarianism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian absolutism is alien to class analysis.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Holloway describes competition among states and capitals as capital's discipline over labour, not a source of human progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; state suppression of parties is disfavoured.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; domination is the core concept, though republican reform of the state is not the aim.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; separation of the political is a fetishised form.

vanguard-party.rationale: Holloway rejects Lenin's claim that consciousness comes to workers from outside, saying knowledge-about is power-over, and the OM1 editors criticise the Leninist party's claim to apply historical laws.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from the stress on labour's side in class antagonism; adherents would back the poor's needs but not as a state-delivered programme.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing privatisation is a policy question the sources never address, and it divides adherents between tenant interests and decommodified housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour struggle is central, so legal restriction is opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is explained by the separation of producers from the means of doing and by permanent primitive accumulation, not by population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Holloway calls the state's ordering of citizens and foreigners racist; the cohesion claim itself is not discussed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to representative politics may incline to it but not stated.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency repression by the state is inferred to be rejected given the view of the state as a form of domination over labour.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; adherents could see price controls as a gain won against capital or as an administrative management of the market.

party-controls-media.rationale: The critique of the party form and of power-over rules out party control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of armed forces is part of the state-socialist model that Holloway and the school reject.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with anti-hierarchy but limited to reform.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Holloway treats the party as a disciplining, hierarchising form that channels revolt into power-building, so binding party discipline is what he rejects.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is a state form of capital; not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the military is a state-power question the sources skip; inferred rejection from anti-state and anti-hierarchy commitments.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is never addressed; mild disagreement inferred from the general hostility to hierarchical authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is not discussed; it is inferred to be rejected on materialist and anti-hierarchy grounds.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Internationalist heritage via Luxemburg, but not stated in the sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship is not discussed; state moral policing is inferred to conflict with autonomy and critical theory.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Electoral term rules belong to the parliamentary politics that adherents regard as secondary; inferred mild disagreement with entrenching rulers.

recall-officials.rationale: Holloway's model of delegation rests on instant recall of those mandated, which applies to any elected official.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed; adherents oppose militarism but treat any state's foreign policy as a capital form.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mandatory home ownership is a property-owner model that sits poorly with a critique of property, but adherents have no stated view.

people-in-arms.rationale: Holloway values the Zapatistas as an armed community rather than an army, but he does not discuss replacing professional armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romanticising rural life is not part of the sources' concerns; inferred mild disagreement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a state-building aim the sources do not take up; internationalism makes adherents cool toward it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are largely academic and opposed to anti-intellectualism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emancipatory, anti-hierarchical outlook.

death-penalty.rationale: Never discussed; state killing is inferred to be rejected given the view of the state as a form of domination.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild support from the emancipatory orientation, with the state school's role viewed critically.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The sources never discuss it; a materialist, critical outlook is inferred to reject it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would be torn between anti-censorship and critique of commodified sexuality.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed, but the critique of the state's citizen/foreigner distinction suggests rejecting descent-based exclusion.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild support for the autonomy of minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no settled view on legal exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild agreement from the anti-conformist, autonomy-centred outlook.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred mild agreement from opposition to austerity against labour and to the discipline of capital.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Political forms are tied to economic forms, so political independence alone is insufficient; inferred from form analysis.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making is a state-form matter the sources skip; adherents favour assemblies from below but not constitutional design as such.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmentalist dictatorship contradicts the emphasis on self-determination and the critique of state-led accumulation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is a state-to-state mechanism the sources never discuss; adherents have no settled view.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are a state power instrument; inferred rejection from anti-militarism and anti-state commitments.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election design is outside the concerns of the sources; no clear stance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not discussed; independence insulates money from democratic pressure, which adherents would regard as a fetishised form, inferred mild disagreement.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims by states are not discussed; internationalists lean toward not treating land as a national possession.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is tied to exploitation, not justified by common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Holloway says the seizure of state power was the defeat of the soviets and that communist governments did little to create a self-determining society, which fits the view that the USSR reproduced capitalist forms.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The sources are silent on environmental regulation; adherents are neither for nor against by principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; military alliances are state forms.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not discussed; adherents give no stated view on annexation law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would be wary of empowering the state against religion as of religious power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state symbolism is not discussed; the unifying-symbol notion is inferred to be disfavoured.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: State military force against regions is inferred to be rejected given the anti-state stance.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view on special-status regions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine kingship is inferred to be rejected on materialist and anti-hierarchy grounds.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not discussed; a regressive-leaning tax design is inferred mildly disfavoured from class-based views.

character-from-environment.rationale: The school treats the individual as constituted in social relations, and Bonefeld calls society fundamentally humans in their social relations.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule unbound by law is inferred to be rejected as an arbitrary form of domination, though law itself is criticised as capital's form.

space-expansion.rationale: Not discussed; mild disagreement inferred since it is a capital-driven expansion project, not an emancipatory goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed; inferred mild disagreement since few-and-many rule frames class rule as a constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader worship contradicts the article's rejection of leader/led hierarchy and stress on self-organisation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed; no settled view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The school does not treat socialism as a stage with a ruling party, so the Maoist question does not arise in its texts.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not discussed; adherents support land for those who work it in principle but the state-led redistribution form is doubted, so left split.

refugee-return.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from the criticism of the citizen/foreigner distinction and solidarity with the displaced.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is inferred to be rejected as nationalist state-building contrary to internationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: State punishment of belief is inferred to be rejected on grounds of autonomy.

women-must-cover.rationale: State compulsion over dress is inferred to be rejected as coercive domination.

common-currency.rationale: Not discussed; money is a form of capital either way, and currency union is inferred mildly disfavoured as a state-capital arrangement.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic or linguistic political union is inferred to be rejected as alien to class internationalism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view on minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would support solidarity and mobility, with no stated position on this strategy question.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The editors reject causal or teleological determinism and hold that class struggle drives history, with structures as modes of existence of that struggle rather than causes.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is a liberal-state measure to preserve competition, which the critique of capital does not treat as a goal; inferred mild disagreement.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bonefeld criticises bailouts for socialising debt to protect profit, yet he also rejects reforms of finance as a remedy, so the statement's policy frame leaves no clear answer.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not discussed; both majority rule and courts are state forms, so adherents have no clear side.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas inside state bodies are not discussed; adherents have no settled view.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs reject the world market, which the sources treat as the horizon; inferred disagreement.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would welcome standards as gains but regard trade agreements as capital's instruments, so left split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; the sources do not address motivation under socialism beyond abolishing wage labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Holloway criticises a century of guerrilla and party militarisation and says insurrectionary or military strategies reproduce the hierarchy of the army.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred from egalitarian opposition to inherited rank.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Civilizational centring of teaching is inferred mildly disfavoured by the internationalist outlook.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage is inferred to be rejected as domination, and conflicts with self-determination.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching national pride is inferred to be rejected given the internationalist critique of the nation-state form.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not discussed; adherents generally favour redress but have no stated view on this tool, inferred mild disagreement.

public-money-creation.rationale: Who issues money is not discussed; since the critique is of money as a form, moving its creation to a public body is not a goal, though adherents have no stated view.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The editors say capital recomposes itself by reintegrating labour and Bonefeld rejects objective laws of collapse, though Holloway stresses capital's crises as a sign of its dependence on labour.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating imperial-era influence is inferred to be rejected as an extension of state power.

delink-world-market.rationale: Holloway argues that national development strategies rest on assumptions that no longer hold, since states are moments of global capital, so national delinking is no route to emancipation.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; labour dependency of capital is universal in the theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not discussed; discrimination by owners is inferred to be rejected on egalitarian grounds and as propertied power.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Bonefeld says formal rights invert into guarantees of exploitation, so entrenching them as the limit on government is only mildly disfavoured.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view.

elective-rulers.rationale: Choosing rulers by election is the representative form Holloway criticises, but adherents have no stated stance on inheritance versus election.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; consensus decision-making may attract autonomist groups, but no source states it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from the endorsement of revolution and refusal.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not discussed; parliamentary supremacy is an institution of the representative democracy criticised, so mild disagreement inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred, no source states it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Elite paternalism is inferred to be rejected, since the aim is abolishing class rather than charity from it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The unity of theory and practice and the demand for revolution here and now imply rejecting withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School influence makes this congenial, but the Open Marxist texts read here do not analyse mass culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not named; the sources emphasise structure as class struggle, leaving the cultural-consent claim unstated.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Holloway rejects centre-periphery dependency accounts because all states sit at the capitalist pole of one global class relation, rather than poor nations being exploited by rich ones.

native-born-offices.rationale: Citizen-only reservation of offices is inferred to be rejected given the criticism of the citizen/foreigner line.

party-own-road.rationale: The article criticises the party form itself, so national party autonomy is not the question adherents ask; inferred mild disagreement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not discussed; no settled view on development strategy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist territorial demands are inferred to be rejected as nationalist.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Zapatismo is cited approvingly, but political leadership by descent is inferred to be unresolved for adherents.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not discussed; anti-fascism is a general commitment, but adherents distrust constitution-writing, so mild support inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not discussed; adherents criticise state Marxism but resist equating it with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical claim not addressed, but adherents' emphasis on class and unfree labour implies rejecting it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not discussed; mild disagreement inferred from the critical orientation.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not discussed; mild disagreement inferred since capitalist forms are treated as universal in the world market.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political army is inferred to be rejected as a state apparatus of domination.

paid-care-work.rationale: Mariarosa Dalla Costa's OM3 chapter treats women as unwaged workers in a waged society, building on the wages-for-housework tradition.

office-by-exam.rationale: Exam-selected officialdom keeps hierarchy and expertise, so mild disagreement inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not discussed; national protection of capital is inferred mildly disfavoured by internationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from an emancipatory outlook.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Holloway favours delegates who are instantly recallable and cites the Zapatista principle of commanding by obeying.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private market accounts replace collective provision with capital markets, inferred to be rejected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no clear stance on tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not discussed; a representative-institution detail on which adherents have no stance.

single-official-language.rationale: Not discussed; compelled monolingualism is inferred mildly disfavoured.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalist land restrictions are inferred to be rejected by internationalism.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no settled legal view.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not discussed explicitly; mild agreement inferred from the critique of commodity fetishism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State sponsorship of foreign proxies is inferred to be rejected as imperial power politics.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power invasion of an ally is inferred to be rejected as imperial domination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred, though it is class power generally and not lobbying as such.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: State control of NGOs is inferred mildly disfavoured as an expansion of state powers.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; state population policy is inferred mildly disfavoured.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; adherents are split between anti-gentrification and anti-exclusion.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; guarantees labour as discipline.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; the liberal view that democracy brings peace is inferred mildly rejected as treating the state form as benign.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Bonefeld treats law as resting on law-making violence and committing individuals to property, and Holloway refuses the legitimacy of power-over, so legal obligation as such carries no moral weight.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; adherents oppose imperialism but support solidarity across borders, so left split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not discussed; industrial over craft organisation would suit class-wide unity, but no source states it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Bonefeld's essay analyses the idea of a hidden minority conspiring against the nation as the antisemitic rumour that personifies capitalism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred from critique of state-conferred forms.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred, with scepticism toward legal rights as forms.

informal-organisation.rationale: The school favours self-organisation over parties and unions, though Holloway's model is open assemblies and councils rather than small closed groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; both are state law, so the question is not of interest, inferred mild disagreement via anti-nationalism.

religious-nation.rationale: A national community defined by faith is inferred to be rejected as anti-internationalist.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary hierarchy among states is inferred to be rejected as domination.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stance on fiscal federalism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not stated; the sources do not take up the distinction.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not discussed; adherents are communists in aim, if hostile to state socialism, so reject defeating it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not discussed; the mix preserves market forms, inferred mild disagreement.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; Marx's thesis but Open Marxism sources say nothing.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Bonefeld rejects any telos in history and calls the idea of history as a becoming of socialism absurd, so capitalism is not treated as a progressive stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Dalla Costa ties women's unwaged position to capitalist development, but the other Open Marxists say little about gender.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no settled view between state provision and autonomous communal care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic nationalism is inferred to be rejected.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The article favours communes and autonomous self-organisation, so small self-governing communities are mildly favoured though not detailed.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement against minorities is inferred to be rejected.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Adherents reject capitalism and state socialism but aim at communism, so the statement's framing is inferred mildly rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Primacy of historic claims over others is inferred to be rejected as nationalism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Bonefeld writes about Nazi antisemitism and its persistence after Auschwitz as historical fact that critical theory must explain.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: State repression is inferred to be rejected on emancipatory grounds.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Holloway rejects power-over and the party-state, so suppressing independent organisation is the opposite of self-determination.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: State punishment of speech or belief is inferred to be rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial extraction is inferred to be rejected as domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious doctrine the sources never discuss; adherents lean against religious-law duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious legitimacy is not an Open Marxist category; inferred rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Holloway's central aim is social self-determination of our own doing, and Bonefeld calls for a democracy of and in the street.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred from the unity of class struggle with other social relations.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from emancipatory orientation.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from autonomy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not discussed; adherents treat the class antagonism as fundamental, so inferred mildly disagree.

alienated-labor.rationale: Holloway holds that doing is always in revolt against labour and names the subordination of concrete to abstract labour as the core problem of capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: A culture-essentialist claim is inferred to be rejected by internationalists.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Divine authority is inferred to be rejected on materialist grounds.

social-market-economy.rationale: Bonefeld's work on ordoliberalism argues that the social market economy rests on a strong coercive state that produces market liberty, which he critiques rather than proposes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred from the aim of abolishing the state.

rich-first.rationale: Step-by-step unequal growth is inferred to be rejected as a justification of exploitation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not discussed; adherents oppose all state blocs, with no stated stance on neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule is inferred to be rejected as hierarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Money reform leaves value and abstract labour in place, and Holloway says cooperative forms within markets keep capitalist constraints; Open Marxist texts do not discuss mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild support from opposition to capital's discipline over labour.

property-franchise.rationale: Property-based voting is inferred to be rejected as class rule.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not discussed; ecofeminist link is not stated in the sources.

reification.rationale: Bonefeld writes that definite social relations assume the form of relations between things, and Holloway makes fetishism and defetishisation the core of his book.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Bonefeld says formal rights and freedoms are the form in which exploitation exists, so legal freedoms mean little under class domination.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Bonefeld treats the rule of law as the state's way of containing class antagonism, so standing law is not an ideal, though he does not defend rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial exclusion is inferred to be rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would be indifferent to the medium.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: State restrictions are inferred to be rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Bonefeld's critique of personified anti-capitalism and antisemitism rejects targeting a minority as the face of economic power.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; random assemblies are a state-adjacent device, while Holloway favours direct democracy, so left split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Not discussed; adherents take no stance.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not discussed directly; mild agreement inferred from the critique of property as the form of exploitation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not discussed; adherents oppose militarism yet support equality, so left split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State promotion of belief is inferred to be rejected as coercive.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not discussed; mild agreement inferred from the aim of abolishing the state and its coercive forms.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not discussed; consociational design is not an Open Marxist concern.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Charity is inferred to be rejected as class paternalism.

term-limits.rationale: Not discussed; a parliamentary rule adherents don't prioritise.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not discussed; direct democracy sympathies leave it open.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from emancipation.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from equality.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from criticism of the citizen/foreigner line.

rent-control.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated stance on housing market tools.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed; hostility to property forms is mild, but intellectual property is not addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements are inferred to be rejected as hierarchical and nationalist.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from anti-militarism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from anti-militarism.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view on state recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; Holloway's anti-labour view and the value critique make the labour framing ambiguous.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism is not Open Marxist; revolution is endorsed, so mild disagreement inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National mythology is inferred to be rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stance on this specific claim.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not discussed; open categories echo the anti-reification approach, but no source states it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: National martyr cult is inferred to be rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Spiritual politics conflicts with the materialist critique.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not discussed; mild disagreement inferred from an anti-nationalist focus.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Bonefeld argues that blaming a minority for economic power falsely splits a productive nation from rootless finance and slides into antisemitism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not discussed; ethnic-territorial design is inferred mildly disfavoured.

independent-unions.rationale: Not discussed; autonomy from state and party fits the article's stance, so mild support inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Self-emancipation is required, but Holloway rejects the working class taking power and treats class identity as something to overcome, so the statement's wording only partly fits.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not discussed; no stance on municipal versus private services.

second-chamber.rationale: Not discussed; a detail of representative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Not discussed; communal property may attract adherents but is not stated.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Holloway calls for a commune of communes or council of councils, built from local assemblies and neighbourhood councils rather than a state centre.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; the wage form is a target of abolition and the family-wage model is gendered, so mild disagreement inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from the anti-surveillance stance.

person-over-state.rationale: Bonefeld's ideal is a society where humanity is purpose not means, but the school would reject the claim that the state exists to serve the person.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not discussed; mild disagreement inferred from the autonomy emphasis.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race-based political organising is inferred to be rejected as dividing class struggle, though adherents have no stated stance.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not discussed; adherents oppose state wars generally, with no stance on defensive ones.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Open Marxism's treatment of the nation-state as a form of capitalist social relations and Holloway's rejection of a national route to change.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the school's critique of state-defined identity categories and its stress on class as a negative relation; separate electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Holloway's argument is against the state and the citizen/foreigner distinction; a narrative of foreign plots against the country would cut against that, though it is not stated.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the school's support for decommodified goods; it distrusts the state as provider, so agreement is mild and unstated.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from Bonefeld's view that the state and money are forms of capital's social relations; a pricing remedy would work inside capital instead of opposing it. Not discussed directly.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist concern with the destructive dynamic of capital; the sources do not discuss the environment.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The school treats social categories as open and class as the main antagonism, and gives no basis for weighting a gendered outlook; inferred, not stated.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the state and militarised power; the sources do not discuss arms levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Holloway's call for direct democracy and rejection of rule by state elites; diplomacy is not discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: Holloway treats the era of national insulation from capital flows as the basis of a Keynesian welfare state that cannot be restored by state reform; controls themselves are not discussed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Bonefeld treats the state as a form of capitalist social relations, so a state monopoly on force is not something the school would defend; this is inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The school draws on Luxemburgist and council-communist anti-war traditions and refuses the state's claims on workers; refusal is inferred as welcome.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Bonefeld sees union and welfare gains as won by struggle but integrating, so adherents would back workers' collective organisation while doubting its limits.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would see top-ups as an accommodation that subsidises low wages, so they split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Bonefeld criticises state-imposed discipline of capital and austerity as forms of authoritarian liberal statecraft; binding fiscal rules are inferred to be opposed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The school is not reformist about global institutions; it would favour poorer countries' struggles but doubts that rule changes help, so it is inferred neutral.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Holloway agrees the state must not be taken over and wants it replaced by a commune of communes, but he rejects insurrectionary or military strategies of seizing or smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Holloway insists there is no blueprint for revolution and cites the Zapatista principle of asking as we walk, though capitalism is not one of the options.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The school's critique of value and commodity forms suggests it would reject pricing nature as capital; this is inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The school aims at abolishing states and class rather than celebrating nations; an enduring sacred nation is inferred to be rejected.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Debt is treated as a mechanism of capitalist discipline, so cancellation is inferred as welcome.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not discussed; adherents attend to class relations over regional ones and also draw on autonomist and anti-colonial thinking.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The school treats human subjectivity as socially constituted and historically open, so a fixed nature as the basis of dignity is inferred to be rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would favour decommodified media but distrust the state as funder.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist treatment of religion as a form of alienated social relations; the sources do not discuss religious truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Adherents would back farmers' security but distrust state guarantees as integrating struggle into capital; the sources are silent.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the school's anti-state and anti-militarist stance, which sees states and their arms as forms of capitalist power.

workers-own-party.rationale: Holloway argues the substitution of the class by the party is inscribed in the party form itself and rejects the party as the vehicle for insubordination.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to emancipation from oppression; the sources do not discuss the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to abolishing class and other hierarchies; the sources do not discuss inheritance law.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not a theme in the sources, and nothing in the core principles fixes a position on language naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the school sees law and courts as forms of the capitalist state, so it would not make private suits the answer, though it opposes polluters.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the state and of hierarchical authority, which extends to chiefly power.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; adherents would oppose capitalist environmental harm but distrust state coercion of freedom.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from Bonefeld's view of criminal law and punishment as part of the capitalist state form.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state coercion and national borders as forms of capitalist social relations.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from class solidarity, which favours union-wide dues, though Open Marxism also distrusts unions as forms of capital.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its rejection of the state and of citizenship as a bourgeois form of exclusion, so it opposes extra barriers to voting.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its call to abolish the state: it gives no religion legal privilege, though the question is outside its texts.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Holloway argues that electing someone to speak on our behalf separates representatives from the represented and extends capital, so competitive elections do not make a society democratic.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its libertarian, anti-patriarchal emancipatory stance.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to state power and its stress on self-organisation and open communication.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: it sees welfare as a form of the capital relation, but a cash scheme that replaces it would still cut provision, so it disagrees mildly.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its emancipatory aims, though it regards formal political rights as limited forms.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view of religion as ideology, held mildly because class relations are its focus.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its view of social categories as historically constituted forms rather than natural facts.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of the state as an agent of emancipation, which counts against state-run bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The school treats property and value as fetishised forms of class relations to be abolished, so a first-claim title to land or resources would be rejected as a capitalist form.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its view of the state and law as forms of capitalist social relations, so courts of states are not seen as neutral; not discussed in the sources.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from a materialist, critical Marxism that rejects dogma; the sources do not discuss scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on self-organisation and autonomy; the texts do not discuss gender in Indigenous self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The school rejects state socialism and Holloway says the state is incompatible with self-determination, so a bureaucratic planned state is not something to defend.

indirect-election.rationale: Holloway's council of councils implies higher bodies of delegates drawn from lower assemblies, rather than direct popular election of officials.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from its aim of abolishing the state and its privileges; religion is not addressed in the sources.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; it rejects the state as a form to be captured, but also values self-organisation, so no clear position.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; it opposes nationalism and the state, so the question is outside its terms.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; it rejects state borders in principle but offers no view on post-colonial boundaries.

simple-living.rationale: Holloway's refusal and anti-capitalism are not an ethic of limited needs; the sources do not discuss it.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred only that it opposes state control of movement, against which it favours self-organisation.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to the state and militarism: it rejects conscription, and the statement is satisfied by applying it to neither sex.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Bonefeld treats the rooted national community bound to its soil as the ideological counterpart of antisemitism, and Holloway rejects nationalism.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Killing without trial is state violence of the kind the school opposes; drug policy is not discussed.

close-ties-china.rationale: The school treats all states as moments of global capital and does not choose between great powers, so it is indifferent to this alignment.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Protecting co-nationals abroad presupposes the national identity that Holloway rejects; the texts do not address it.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Compensating others for appropriation keeps resources as property; Holloway opposes property as appropriation of doing, so the formula is alien to the school, though it is not discussed.

self-ownership.rationale: Bonefeld treats the worker free to sell her own labour power as a capitalist form, so self-ownership is not a value of the school.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is not a theme of the school's texts.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Means-testing is not discussed; Holloway treats dependence on state subsidies as a limit on autonomy, and targeting would deepen state classification.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Holloway rejects parties, but the statement's appeal to a leader conflicts with his rejection of representation and power-over.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Bonefeld rejects explaining capitalism by greedy or well-connected capitalists rather than by social relations, so crony privilege is not the issue for him.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religion is not discussed, but organising politics by identity runs against Holloway's call to move beyond identities.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Holloway and Bonefeld reject appeals to rooted ancestral identity; the statement's combination is not discussed.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The school's emancipatory aim and Dalla Costa's feminism support this, though divorce law is not discussed.

national-resource-control.rationale: National control assumes the national state form Holloway rejects, though the school opposes appropriation by capital; it is not discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: the school treats exchange and distribution as forms of capitalist exploitation, so judging them by how they arose would be a liberal fetish.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Bonefeld rejects the good industry/bad finance split and regulatory fixes, so a Tobin-style tax would look like a reform that leaves capital intact; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: the sources treat capitalist forms as the central problem but do not claim racism has ceased to matter, and they analyse antisemitism as a live danger.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The school treats law and rights as forms of capitalist social relations rather than moral standards binding in conscience, so natural-law talk is foreign to it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: Open Marxism wants to end abstract labour under capital, which favours less paid work, but it does not endorse technological fixes within capitalism.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: states are moments of global capital, so a world of competing power centres is no goal for a school that wants to go beyond state forms.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Bonefeld reads value as the form of abstract labour in capitalism, in line with Marx's critique of political economy, though as social form rather than a technical theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Holloway and Bonefeld treat nationalism and the national state as forms of capital, and condemn blood-and-soil politics.

material-over-identity.rationale: The school rejects affirming identities, including the identity of workers, so it does not frame the choice this way; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Open Marxists reject both the vanguard party and the state and treat markets and money as fetishised capitalist forms.

missingStatements.text: The laws of capitalist development are not objective necessities but the fetishised form of ongoing class struggle.
missingStatements.rationale: Bonefeld and the Open Marxism editors reject deterministic laws of capital and call them forms of the movement of class struggle.

missingStatements.text: Socialist change should aim to abolish the state rather than capture it.
missingStatements.rationale: The school holds that the state is a form of capitalist social relations so the goal is abolition, and Holloway argues for change without taking power.

missingStatements.text: The working class should struggle to abolish itself as a class rather than to affirm its identity as workers.
missingStatements.rationale: Holloway writes that we struggle not as working class but against being working class, and Bonefeld treats class as a critical concept for the dissolution of class society.
missingStatements.declined: Statement bank frozen on 2026-10-22, before the people audits: no new statements are added.

notes: Bonefeld's Critical Theory and the Critique of Political Economy was read through the Lotz and Cammack reviews, which quote it with page numbers, rather than in full. Holloway is the most explicit on politics (state, party, councils, borders); Bonefeld is more cautious about prescriptions and calls critical theory entirely negative. Critics such as Stoetzler say Holloway slides from negativity into affirming movements and identities, and Trotskyists such as Hearse say the anti-party stance abandons the fight over government. The anti-nationalist and anti-conspiracy answers rest on Bonefeld's Adorno- and Postone-influenced critique of personified anti-capitalism, which adherents broadly share, while his position on Israel is not shared by all.
